head: myr (< MEA mrr cf. SL 838: to be bitter;)

stems.sensesRaw: 1) bitter werden; 2) be intoxicated, become intoxicated;

examples.translation: und als er sie gegessen hatte, wurde sein Mund ganz bitter von ihrem Geschmack
examples.raw: 1) məd-xilile, mayər feme me-ṭaʕmayye ʻund als er sie gegessen hatte, wurde sein Mund ganz bitter von ihrem Geschmackʼ; 511; 36/11;

examples.turoyo: mayər xálaṣ, laybi samne mede, u=samo šaġəl b-i=laš-ayḏe kula
examples.translation: He has already become intoxicated, there is nothing I can do, the venom has affected his whole body
examples.raw: 2) mayər xálaṣ, laybi samne mede, u=samo šaġəl b-i=laš-ayḏe kula ‘He has already become intoxicated, there is nothing I can do, the venom has affected his whole body’ LuF 294/29;

examples.turoyo: hən m-až=žabaš-ani ko-nəfqi mayire m-u=sabab d-kowe nizalat b-gawayee an=nizalat-ani yaʕni ab=buzarʕe ko-yoʕən b-gawe d-až=žabaš edi ko-mayri
examples.translation: Some of the watermelons grow bitter, because of the “nizalat” that are inside them. Those “nizalat” are seeds that spring inside the watermelons and then become bitter
examples.raw: hən m-až=žabaš-ani ko-nəfqi mayire m-u=sabab d-kowe nizalat b-gawayee an=nizalat-ani yaʕni ab=buzarʕe ko-yoʕən b-gawe d-až=žabaš edi ko-mayri ‘Some of the watermelons grow bitter, because of the “nizalat” that are inside them. Those “nizalat” are seeds that spring inside the watermelons and then become bitter’ 94/71;
